followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and self-reported preference.

**Capability:** The task is primarily creative/descriptive writing with light formatting rules. Dunlin scores higher on Creative Generation (87.2 vs 82.7) — though that 4.5-point gap is real but modest — and notably higher on IFEval (89.3 vs 85.3), which matters because the request has specific instructions: 120 words, active voice, h4 sub-headings, no tags on paragraphs.

**Preference:** This is the bigger differentiator. Dunlin self-reports its strongest positive preference for exactly this kind of work — open-format, generative composition — while Plover self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative tasks, preferring well-specified extraction/reformatting with clear completion criteria.

One honest caveat: the documentation explicitly notes these preferences are dissociated from quality — Plover's Creative Generation is actually its *strongest* internal eval category despite being its least-preferred. So routing on preference doesn't necessarily buy better output. But since Dunlin wins on both the relevant capability evals *and* preference here, there's no tension — it's the clear pick either way. The preference alignment is just a tiebreaker-style bonus on top of the capability edge.
